name: Shiphrah and Puah, the midwives
charge: Fearing God and not doing as the king of Egypt commanded them
summary: Pharaoh commanded the Hebrew midwives to kill every son at the birthstool: the fruit of the body attacked at the source. They feared God more than the king and saved the men children alive, and answered that the daughters of Israel are not as the women of the nations. Because they feared God, he dealt well with them and made them houses.
offenseFull: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one named Shiphrah and the other Puah, and told them that when they did the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women and saw them upon the stools, if it were a son they were to kill him, and if a daughter, she should live (Exodus 1:15-16). This is what dealing wisely looks like when it reaches the cradle: the male children killed at birth, the fruit of the body cursed at the source, which is one of the named curses on the nation (Deuteronomy 28:18). Spiritual Egypt does the same thing by other means, through abortion and through a system built to take the sons, with poverty and drugs brought into the community and the school to prison pipeline waiting at the end of it. They are trying to stop the prophets from ever coming up.

But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive (Exodus 1:17). That is the apostles’ rule long before the apostles: we ought to obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29). Two women stood between a king’s order and a nation’s sons. Called to account for why they had saved the men children alive, they answered that the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, being lively, and delivered before the midwives come in to them (Exodus 1:18-19): the daughters of Israel are not as the women of the nations. The record does not rebuke the answer.
judgmentFull: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very mighty; and it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses (Exodus 1:20-21). The blessing and the reason for it are stated in the same breath: not because the plan worked, but because they feared God. The increase they risked their own lives to protect is set down in the same verse as their reward, and the whole nation that came out of Egypt came through the hands they refused to use.

Pharaoh’s plot did not succeed. His next order, that every son born be cast into the river, is what put the deliverer into his own house, where Pharaoh’s daughter drew him out of the water and paid his own mother to nurse him (Exodus 1:22; Exodus 2:5-10). The names of these two women are written in the book; the name of the Pharaoh who commanded them is not.

text.text: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep.
But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?
And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.
Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.
Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.
And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
